### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close #31772

### What is changed and how it works?

- Two new methods added to `TxnManager`
  - `GetTxnScope` returns the scope for current txn. `TxnScope` is used by local transaction
  - `GetReadReplicaScope` returns the read replica scope. `ReadReplicaScope` is used to read other replica instead of leader.
- Stale read will always return a `kv.GlobalScope` for `TxnScope` to skip local txn check.
- Stale read will always use local scope to do replica read
- For other providers, if local txn is enabled or closest read is enabled, we should use local txn's scope to do replica read.

issue_context.title: Decouple the term TxnScope from the Stale Read code
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement

Since the two features, Stale Read and Local Txn were developed together, the former borrows many of the concepts from the latter. `TxnScope` should be a term referring to the Global/Local Transaction scopes specifically. However, in the code of Stale Read, `TxnScope` is also used widely to indicate the TiKV locality, which brings some confusion into the code readability.

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/ab30467384b7f18f1c2af2e34f37cf00f20f2d54/distsql/request_builder.go#L51-L75
 
We should decouple the `TxnScope` from the Stale Read code to make it more clear when we try to write some code that is related to the locality of the TiKV store.

review_comments: Should this have a higher priority than `local txn check`?
I think they are both equal because when local txn is enabled, the "closest" replica is the "local" replica. And local txn check is a hard constraint that seems to be have "higher" priority.
